sections.h2: Where is the Swain County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The office is in the Courthouse Building at 101 Mitchell Street in Bryson City, NC 28713. Letters should use P.O. Box 1183. The county lists (828) 488-9273, extension 2205, for questions.

Staff are at the counter weekdays, 8:30 am until 5:00 pm. Marriage licenses stop half an hour sooner, at 4:30 pm. The office also publishes an email address, RegisterofDeeds@swaincountync.gov, for questions before you travel.

Census QuickFacts shows 14,024 people on 527.73 square miles of land, about 26.8 people per square mile. Everyone with a deed to record, whether the parcel is in town or on a mountain road, uses this one counter.

sections.h2: What documents does the Swain County register take in?
sections.html:
The office records real property documents and also keeps the county's vital records. The county page lists these categories, which cover nearly everything a seller will meet:

  • Deeds, contracts, leases, mortgages and deeds of trust.
  • Cancellations of deeds of trust, maps and plats, and powers of attorney.
  • Assumed names, UCC filings, articles of incorporation and corporate mergers.
  • Bankruptcy orders, judgments, marriage settlements and military discharges.

The same office collects the revenue stamps, meaning the excise tax, on deeds being recorded. It also issues certified copies of birth, death and marriage certificates. Certified vital record copies are $10.00 each and uncertified copies $1.00 each, according to the county page. Those fees apply to vital records, so they are separate from the schedule for recording a deed.

sections.h2: What will recording cost in Bryson City?
sections.html:
Deed recording prices come from a single state schedule, G.S. 161-10, with a short list of per-page and per-document items. Swain County links a recording fee sheet and a document standards sheet from its register page, and both are worth reading before you send a paper deed.

The sheet is the full list, and payment comes before filing. Sellers rarely write this check, because recording of the deed and the lender's security instrument normally sits with the buyer. Your purchase contract decides who bears it.

Fee items to expect when documents are recorded in Swain County
DocumentRate printed in the statuteSource
Mortgage or deed of trustPriced on its own, higher schedule that starts with 35 pages includedG.S. 161-10
Plat$21.00 per sheetG.S. 161-10
Nonstandard document add-on$25.00G.S. 161-10
Extra instruments in one document$10.00 eachG.S. 161-10

sections.h2: Who pays the deed stamps in a Swain County sale?
sections.html:
Owing it falls on the seller. Under G.S. 105-228.30, whoever transfers title pays the register first, and only then is the deed recorded.

The amount appears on your settlement statement, and the closer carries it to Bryson City with the deed. It scales with the price, so request the exact number instead of estimating.

sections.h2: How do home values in Swain County look?
sections.html:
Owner-occupied homes in Swain County carry a $207,000 median value in the 2020-2024 QuickFacts survey period. Owners live in 72.7% of them, and the median rent is $742. Housing units numbered 8,951 as of July 2025, and permits totaled 94 for 2025.

QuickFacts also reports that 30.6% of residents identify as American Indian and Alaska Native alone, the highest share among the four counties in the table the Census page compares. If a tract has an unusual ownership history, ask your title company early what it needs to see.

Households earn a median $52,349, and 22.0% of people are past 65. A clean chain of title at the register speeds up any closing.

sections.h2: What vital records and notary help does Swain County offer sellers?
sections.html:
A seller settling an estate often needs a death certificate, and the register issues them. The county lists four ways to ask: upload a photo of your ID on its premium site, email a photo, fax a request, or mail it with a copy of your ID. In person, bring a state ID, driver license, military ID or passport.

Under G.S. 130A-93, as the county summarizes it, those entitled to a certified copy include yourself, a spouse, a sibling, a child or step-child, a parent or step-parent, a grandparent or grandchild, and an authorized agent or attorney with proof. Requesting a record by fraud is a felony under G.S. 130A-26A.

The county tax office, in the same building, offers notary service for cash only, at $8.00 for the first signature, $9.00 for a second signer and $10.00 for more than two. The tax department closes for lunch from 1:30 to 2:00 and shuts at 4:30 pm. Confirm those times before a signing trip.

sections.h2: Can I search Swain County land records online?
sections.html:
Yes. The county provides a remote access site for land records with two modes. The full system lets you search by grantor or grantee name, instrument number, or book and page. The imaging system only retrieves deed book images when you enter a book and page.

The county warns that online records are unofficial and that the official records are kept at the register's office. For a certified copy that a court or lender will accept, ask the office itself.

  • Search by name when you do not know the book and page.
  • Use book and page for a direct image of a known deed.
  • Take any reference from the online index to the counter if you need an official copy.

sections.h2: How does the Swain County tax office tie in with a sale?
sections.html:
The tax office sits in the same Courthouse Building, with a separate mailing address of P.O. Box 2321. It splits into an assessor side, which handles values and reappraisal, and a collections side, which handles payment and enforcement. Phone numbers run through (828) 488-9273.

The county tax page says bills go out in July, fall due September 1, and begin collecting interest after January 5. G.S. 105-360 holds the interest schedule.

Swain County's last reappraisal took effect January 1, 2021, and the county tax page notes an eight-year cycle. The county also says a revaluation contractor has been working in the Alarka community. Call the assessor to learn which year applies to you. The county posts a disabled veteran exclusion form and a property tax relief application on that page.

sections.h2: What should my closer confirm in Swain County?
sections.html:
Confirm three things with your closer: that the deed matches the legal description, that the excise tax amount is on the statement, and that outstanding property tax is settled. A buyer will expect unpaid property tax to be paid off, since G.S. 105-355 makes it a charge against the parcel.

  • Ask whether the buyer's lender needs a payoff letter from a prior mortgage.
  • Ask who will carry the signed deed to the register and by what date.
  • Request the recording book and page once the deed is filed.

If the house came through an estate, start with the court clerk. G.S. 28A-25-1 describes an affidavit route for small estates, and land questions belong with an attorney.

faqs.q: When can I visit the Swain County deed office?
faqs.a: Come between 8:30 am and 5:00 pm on a weekday to 101 Mitchell Street in Bryson City. License issuing ends 30 minutes earlier.

faqs.q: How do I search Swain County deeds online?
faqs.a: Use the county's remote access site, which offers a full system search by name, instrument number or book and page, plus an imaging-only mode. Those results are unofficial, so use the office for certified copies.

faqs.q: Which party covers the deed stamps in Swain County?
faqs.a: The seller does, ahead of recording, under G.S. 105-228.30. Your closer will show the figure on the statement.

faqs.q: What does a certified vital record copy cost in Swain County?
faqs.a: Certified copies are $10.00 each and uncertified copies $1.00 each, according to the county page. These fees are for birth, death and marriage records, not deed recordings.

faqs.q: When are Swain County property taxes due?
faqs.a: September 1, with interest starting after January 5 per the county. Ask the Courthouse Building tax office for your bill.
